extra.message: The acct_bundle_thaw_184 function uses pickle.loads() on user-controlled input from request.body or request.GET.get('blob'). This allows arbitrary code execution through insecure deserialization. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload to execute arbitrary commands on the server.

The acct_shell_probe_700 function uses os.system() with user-controlled input from request.GET.get('host') concatenated directly into the command string. This allows command injection. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters like ';', '&&', or '|' to execute arbitrary commands.

The acct_jinja_cast_682 function uses Jinja2 Template with user-controlled input from request.GET.get('fragment'). This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). An attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax like '{{ config }}' or '{{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}' to execute arbitrary code.

extra.message: The acct_dock_shelf_719 function writes request body to a file path constructed using user-controlled input from request.GET.get('name') without proper sanitization. Path traversal sequences like '../' can be used to write files anywhere on the filesystem.

extra.message: The import_contacts function sets a hardcoded password 'changeme123' for newly created users. Hardcoded passwords are a security risk as they are easily guessable and may not be changed by users.

The SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded default value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-me'. If the environment variable is not set, this weak secret will be used, compromising session security and cryptographic operations.
DEBUG mode is enabled by default (DEBUG = True if environment variable not set). Running Django in debug mode in production exposes sensitive information through detailed error pages.
